q: In the running-median design, the lower half lives in a…
why: You need the LARGEST of the lower half quickly, so it's a max-heap.

q: Lower heap holds {1, 3} and upper heap holds {5, 8}. The median is…
why: Equal sizes: average of the tops, (3 + 5) / 2 = 4.

q: Adding one number to the two-heap median structure costs…
why: A constant number of heap pushes/pops.

q: Merging k sorted lists with N elements in total using a heap costs…
why: Every element is pushed and popped once on a heap of size ≤ k.

q: Why push (value, index, node) instead of (value, node)?
options: When values tie, Python compares the next field; ListNode objects can't be compared
why: The unique index breaks ties before Python ever tries to compare nodes.

q: You only need to merge TWO sorted lists. Best approach?
why: A heap adds nothing for k = 2; a simple two-pointer merge is O(n + m).
